title: Relative Clauses with Dative and Prepositions
summary: Extending relative clauses to more complex reference patterns.
whyItMatters: Dative and prepositional relative clauses connect nouns to recipients, tools, locations, and relationships without repetitive sentences.

mentalModel.title: Case comes from the relative clause
mentalModel.content: The antecedent determines gender and number; the verb or preposition inside the relative clause determines case.

mentalModel.title: Keep the preposition attached
mentalModel.content: Place the preposition directly before the relative pronoun.

ruleBlocks.title: Choose dative after dative verbs
ruleBlocks.content: Use dem, der, and denen when the relative-clause verb requires dative.

ruleBlocks.title: Let the preposition determine case
ruleBlocks.content: Use mit dem, für die, an das, von denen, and other required combinations.

ruleBlocks.title: Use denen for dative plural
ruleBlocks.content: The form is independent of noun gender in plural.

ruleBlocks.title: Put the finite verb last
ruleBlocks.content: The prepositional phrase stays inside the relative clause and the finite verb closes it.

sentenceStructure: Match pronoun gender and number to the antecedent.

concepts: use genitive and complex relative reference

comparisons.summary: Products provide tools, users, purposes, and features to link.
Function descriptions become more precise through relative clauses.

examples.de: Das ist der Kunde, dem ich das Gerät empfohlen habe.
examples.en: That is the customer to whom I recommended the device.

examples.de: Die App, mit der man das Gerät steuert, ist kostenlos.
examples.en: The app used to control the device is free.

examples.de: Das ist eine Funktion, für die viele Nutzer extra bezahlen.
examples.en: This is a function for which many users pay extra.

examples.de: Die Modelle, von denen wir gesprochen haben, sind wieder lieferbar.
examples.en: The models we discussed are available again.

examples.de: Die Kollegin, der das Gerät gehört, arbeitet heute nicht.
examples.en: The colleague to whom the device belongs is not working today.

commonMistakes.wrong: die App, die ich mit arbeite
commonMistakes.correct: die App, mit der ich arbeite
commonMistakes.reason: The preposition precedes the relative pronoun.

commonMistakes.wrong: das Gerät, mit dem ich arbeite täglich
commonMistakes.correct: das Gerät, mit dem ich täglich arbeite
commonMistakes.reason: The finite verb closes the clause.

tips: Write the relative clause as a separate sentence first.
Circle the governing verb or preposition.
